name: Busboys & Poets
notes: Full menu and a large patio; opens early for breakfast.

name: Best Buns Bread Company
notes: Bakery; pastries and coffee before a ride.

name: Bluemont Park
notes: Restrooms, water, picnic shelters. Junction with the Custis Trail and the Four Mile Run Trail.

name: Bon Air Memorial Rose Garden
notes: Worth a two-minute detour in May and June.

name: Solace Outpost
address: 444 West Broad Street, Falls Church, VA 22046
notes: Brewery taproom with a large outdoor space and food menu. Occupies the former Mad Fox building.

name: Rarebird Coffee Roasters
address: 230;228 West Broad Street, Falls Church, VA 22046
notes: Small local roaster; order at the counter.

name: Spacebar
address: 709 West Broad Street, Falls Church, VA 22046
notes: Grilled cheese sandwiches and a long craft beer list.

name: The State Theatre
address: 220 North Washington Street, Falls Church, VA 22046
notes: Live music venue in a 1936 cinema.

name: Vienna Inn
notes: Chili dogs and cheap pitchers in a diner-bar that has been on Maple Avenue since 1960.

name: Caffe Amouri
notes: Roasts its own beans. Espresso, drip and pastries.

name: Plaka Grill
notes: Gyros and Greek plates, counter service.

name: Bikes@Vienna
notes: Repairs, tubes, and recumbents. Trek Bicycle and Conte's are also within a few blocks.

name: Vienna caboose & depot
notes: Restored W&OD freight station (now the model railroad museum) and a red caboose. Benches and shade.

name: Caboose Tavern
notes: Caboose Brewing's original taproom, directly off the trail with abundant bike parking. Rotating taps and a farm-to-table menu.

name: Meadowlark Botanical Gardens
notes: NOVA Parks garden with restrooms at the visitor center. Admission fee for the gardens.

name: Cross County Trail junction
coordinate_source: trail point at mile marker (place itself not geocoded)
notes: The 40-mile Gerry Connolly Cross County Trail crosses here.

name: Bike Lane Brewing & Café
off_trail: right on the trail, Sunset Hills Rd
notes: Bike shop, brewery and café in one building at the Sunset Hills crossing. Repairs while you drink.

name: Founding Farmers
notes: Big brunch menu; expect a wait on weekends.

name: Taco Zocalo
notes: Food truck turned taqueria near Bike Lane; cheap and fast.

name: Reston Town Center
off_trail: about 0.5 mi north of the trail
notes: Dozens of restaurants and a public plaza. Ted's Bulletin for pop-tarts and milkshakes.

name: Twisted Sweets & Savory
notes: Hungarian chimney cakes and a sandwich menu that made a national top-100 list; quiet strip-mall spot off Grant St.

name: Weird Brothers Coffee
notes: Roaster and café in the Sunset Park Dr strip, which also has Enatye, Chai Wyy and Crème de la Crop. Reach it by the new path along Herndon Parkway.

name: Enatye Ethiopian Restaurant
notes: Ethiopian platters and vegetarian combos; a NoVA best-restaurants regular.

name: Herndon Depot & caboose
notes: Restored 1857 station, now a small museum. Benches, shade, and the town green.

name: Aslin Beer Co
notes: Small-batch brewery with a lively tasting room, a half block off the trail. Izzy's kitchen inside does a well-liked chicken sandwich.

name: Jimmy's Old Town Tavern
notes: Wings, burgers and a long beer list; TVs for games.

name: Great Harvest Bread Co
notes: Bakery; free bread slices.

name: Sully's Pour House
notes: Bar on Elden Street with a short pub menu.

name: Green Lizard Cycling
off_trail: right on the trail, Lynn St
notes: Bike shop with a coffee bar and beer taps, directly on the trail next to the Herndon depot. Rentals, repairs, and a place to sit.
source: curated: komoot / wanderlog trail highlights (web, 2026); r/bikedc i64koh

name: Dairy Queen
off_trail: right on the trail, Lynn St
notes: Treat-only DQ beside the trail in old town Herndon. A 40-mile round trip for a Blizzard is a r/bikedc tradition.

name: Anita's New Mexico Style Mexican Food
off_trail: right on the trail, Elden St
notes: Local chain known for breakfast burritos and green chile; open early.

name: Wooboi Hot Chicken
notes: Nashville-style hot chicken sandwiches. Weekday lunch hours only; check before riding out.

name: Herndon Community Center
notes: Water fountain and restrooms during opening hours.

name: Crooked Run Fermentation
notes: Crooked Run's Sterling production brewery and taproom, with Señor Ramon Taqueria inside.

name: Joe's Café
notes: Diner-style breakfast and coffee.

name: Old Ox Brewery
notes: Less than ten steps from the trail with ample bike parking. Big taproom, food trucks most days.

name: Lost Rhino Brewing
off_trail: about 2 mi by road, Red Rum Dr
notes: Ashburn's original craft brewery. A real detour from the trail, about two miles each way on roads.

name: Carolina Brothers Pit BBQ
notes: North Carolina pulled pork with a choice of sauces, counter service, outdoor tables.
source: Washingtonian; fxva.com best stops; r/bikedc 1mmr9sa, i64koh

name: Goose Creek bridge
coordinate_source: trail point at mile marker (place itself not geocoded)
notes: Long bridge over Goose Creek with a view of the quarry and the creek valley.

name: Mom's Apple Pie Company
off_trail: right on the trail, Loudoun St
notes: Pie by the slice, a few steps from the trail. Benches outside.

name: Crooked Run Brewing (Market Station)
notes: The original Crooked Run, a small taproom in the Market Station complex a quarter-mile from the trail.

name: Black Hoof Brewery
notes: Lagers and Czech-style beers in downtown Leesburg.

name: Black Walnut Brewery
notes: Shares a building with Kahvila coffee house, so it works as a morning or afternoon stop.

name: Dynasty Brewing
coordinate_source: trail point at mile marker (place itself not geocoded)
notes: Taproom and beer garden in Leesburg.

name: Transition Triathlon
coordinate_source: trail point at mile marker (place itself not geocoded)
notes: Full-service shop. Pedego and Maverick Bicycles are also nearby.

name: South Street Under
notes: Bakery-deli from the Tuscarora Mill team: sandwiches on house bread, a patio, and a cidery next door.

name: Clarks Gap
coordinate_source: trail point at mile marker (place itself not geocoded)
notes: High point of the trail at the ridge crossing west of Leesburg. Long steady climb from the east; freewheel from here to Purcellville.

name: Hamilton Station
address: Washington & Old Dominion Trail, Paeonian Springs, VA 20158
notes: Small trailside parking area at Hamilton Station Road with a bench. No services; the town of Hamilton is a short detour north.

name: Belly Love Brewing
notes: Taproom at the east edge of Purcellville, the first beer after the long climb.

name: Velo Classique
off_trail: right on the trail, O St
notes: Vintage and classic bicycle shop beside the trail; closed Sunday and Monday.

name: Purcellville Train Station
notes: Restored 1904 depot marking the western end of the trail. Restrooms and water nearby in season.

name: Magnolias at the Mill
notes: Sit-down restaurant in a converted feed mill beside the station.

name: Monk's BBQ
notes: Barbecue with a big outdoor patio and local beer on tap.

name: Catoctin Creek Distillery
notes: Rye whiskey tastings and tours in downtown Purcellville.
